messages:
sam: Heads-up: scheduling prod rollout for v2.11.1 in ~10m. Target change: route traffic to llm-flow-v2. Ramp plan: 5% internal-only (dev orgs + staging keys) for 15m -> 25% mobile clients for 20m -> 100% after 1h if health good. Pin router model to cantor-1@2026-03-10. Rollback criteria: sustained 5xx >1% for 5m OR p95 latency +40% OR >10% pod restarts in 10m. Notifying @sre-oncall and @riley.

riley: Can we exclude apac regions for the initial rollout? capacity in apac is tight today.

sam: Good catch. Excluding apac and adding header-based cohort for internal traffic. Also temp lower max_batch_size to 32 for the new route.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollout queued by sam at 1769812345. Actions:
```
/ff set routing/llm-flow-v2 5% --cohort internal --exclude-region apac
/model pin router cantor-1@2026-03-10
/config set router.max_batch_size=32 --path llm-flow-v2
/monitor enable rollout-telemetry routing/llm-flow-v2
```
I'll post heartbeat every 5m.

taylor: Canary pods coming up. see canary-1, canary-2 healthy; canary-3 restarted once during init with OOM. logs: `oom-kill process router-worker (pid 8421) rss 2.8G`

sre-oncall: That single OOM on canary-3 is a red flag given reduced batch size. Recommend hold at 5% and switch canary to debug mode (heap profiles + reduced concurrency) before further ramp. If restarts continue, roll back to 0%.

sam: Hold at 5% then. sam -> deploy-bot: apply debug flags and reduce concurrency to 4 on canaries. Commands:
```
/config set router.debug_heap=true --target canary-*
/config set router.max_concurrency=4 --target canary-*
```

deploy-bot: status @1769812945: routing/llm-flow-v2 at 5% internal-only. Canary-1 healthy, canary-2 healthy, canary-3 restart count=2. Telemetry: p95 +12% vs baseline, 5xx 0.4%. Heap profiles enabled.

taylor: canary-3 restarted again, now 3 restarts in 12m. logs show increased memory growth on cantor-1: `alloc 1.9G -> 2.7G within 60s`. suspect model memory pattern different than baseline.

sre-oncall: Restart threshold exceeded (>10% pod restarts across canaries would be 0.3 pods so this is still concentrated but trend is upward). Recommend immediate soft-drain: set ff to 0% for non-internal cohorts and keep internal traffic pinned while we investigate. Do NOT full-rollback yet; capture traces + heap dumps.

sam: Agreed. Executing soft-drain:
```
/ff set routing/llm-flow-v2 0% --cohort public
/ff set routing/llm-flow-v2 5% --cohort internal
/incident create "canary memory growth llm-flow-v2" --severity medium
```

deploy-bot: action complete at 1769813520 1: routing/llm-flow-v2 public cohorts set to 0%. Internal cohort remains at 5%. Canary traffic drained for public. Incident ticket: INC-2026-1842 created.

riley: Please pull heap profiles and batch-size histograms for the canary window (first 25m). Also capture VM memory slab and page cache metrics. We'll need them for model-team triage.

taylor: Uploading traces + profile link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-1842/profiles. Added a note to reproduce locally with smaller batch sizes and instrumented allocator.

ops-bot: ops-bot: pinned release notes for v2.11.1 back to draft state and muted public announcement. Next steps: model-team to reproduce, possibly try cantor-1 quantized variant or fallback cantor-0@2026-02-20 if model memory pattern confirmed.

sam: Thanks everyone. Scheduling 30m triage sync (standup room) and a short postmortem if we close incident. Will not proceed with any further ramp until canaries stable for 60m.
